### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Jeffries-Lakhani neurodevelopmental syndrome  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.632)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:14630)

**Proposed mechanism:** CRELD1 (HGNC:14630) —DISRUPTS→ ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) (GO:0030430); ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) (GO:0030430) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal heart valve morphology (HP:0001687); ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) (GO:0030430) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in CRELD1 disrupt the ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) pathway, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins. This ER stress and subsequent cellular dysfunction manifest as distinct but overlapping phenotypes, including cardiac abnormalities in MONDO:0011650 and global developmental delay in Jeffries-Lakhani neurodevelopmental syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that pathogenic variants in CRELD1 are exclusively associated with loss-of-function effects in disease A and gain-of-function effects in disease B, or that the disease mechanisms do not converge on the ERAD pathway. _(variant: The presence of common, benign variants in CRELD1 within gnomAD that do not segregate with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CRELD1 in ERAD provides a potential therapeutic target for both conditions, aiming to restore proper protein folding and degradation to alleviate downstream cellular dysfunction and improve patient outcomes.
